# E-ink Usability Checklist: PB Store on the Reader

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for paged lists, touch targets, screen refresh behavior, progress display without animation, plain three-part messages, offline browsing, the states of the app list and the restart wording are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md, constitution 2.1.0, the device-facts table in the spec's Background, and the message rules of feature 002 in `docs/installer-rules.md`). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]` and should be settled in the plan or by editing the spec. The look "of PB Notes feature 010 and PB Cloud" (FR-042) lives in the sibling projects and is not read here; items that depend on it are marked `[Dependency]`. Safety and recovery wording is in `install-safety.md`.

## Paged Lists and Navigation

- [ ] CHK001 Is the number of apps per page, or the rule that fixes it, specified (for example by screen height and row height), and is the order of the list (by name, by catalog order, installed first) defined? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK002 Is it specified where the user lands after returning from a detail page, a plan, a message or a finished operation (the same page, the first page, the page of the app just changed)? [Gap, Spec §Story 1]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the behavior of the page buttons defined at the first and last page and for a list that fits on one page (hidden, disabled, or "page 1 of 1"), so that a disabled control is not mistaken for a broken one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the interactions of search and paging defined (results are paged again, the page resets, the count of matches is shown), including the empty result ("no app matches") and an empty catalog? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-010, §Story 1 scenario 7]
- [ ] CHK005 Is it stated when the search is applied (at each typed letter or on confirm), given that every letter on an e-ink screen with an on-screen keyboard costs a screen update? [Ambiguity, Spec §Story 1 scenario 7]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "Hardware page keys MAY also turn the pages" decided (required, optional, or not for this feature), and is it stated what the page buttons do on the screen when the reader has such keys? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]

## Touch Targets and Legibility

- [ ] CHK007 Is "a clear gap to the next one" quantified, and is it stated which controls the 10 mm rule covers (list rows, page buttons, top-bar icon controls, dialog buttons, the keys of the keyboard shown for the search)? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the 10 mm figure justified or marked as an assumption, and is a way to measure it given that does not depend on a ruler on the real reader (a size in pixels derived from the screen's resolution and size)? [Assumption, Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK009 Are minimum text size and contrast defined for the grey levels of the screen (list text, the one-line description, messages, the plan text), instead of only a size for controls? [Gap, Spec §FR-042]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the top-bar icon controls required to carry a text label or a text description, since an icon alone may not say what Refresh, Search, Settings or About does? [Gap, Spec §FR-042]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the feedback to a tap defined when nothing may animate (what shows that a tap was received, and how fast), and is it consistent with ignoring further taps while an operation runs? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-024]

## Screen Refresh and "No Animation"

- [ ] CHK012 Does the spec define when a partial refresh is allowed and when a full refresh is required (page turn, return from a dialog, after a number of partial refreshes), since the request names partial and full refresh and the spec contains neither term? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "animation" defined well enough to be checked (spinners, blinking cursor, kinetic or continuous scroll, fade, a changing progress bar between figures), including whether the visible flash of a full refresh counts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-017, §FR-042]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "no more often than about every two seconds" replaced by a number with a tolerance, and is it said whether a Cancel tap during a long step is answered at once, outside that limit? [Ambiguity, Measurability, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK015 Is ghosting addressed (a remaining image of the previous screen after dialogs and long lists), for example by a rule for a full refresh at the start of an operation and at its end? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Progress Display

- [ ] CHK016 Is the content of the progress figure defined for each step (download, verification, writing, repair, "Update all"), including what is shown when a step has no known total and what shows overall position such as "app 2 of 3"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017, §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the state of the Cancel control after the commit point specified (hidden, disabled with a reason, or held until finish with a message), and is it consistent with "Cancel until the commit point" and the home-key rule? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK018 Is it specified where and when the screen says that the store switched Wi-Fi on and off again, so that the notice is not lost between progress screens? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK019 Is a rule given for long steps with no visible change (for example verifying a large package), so the user can tell a working reader from a frozen one without animation? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-017]

## Plain Three-Part Messages

- [ ] CHK020 Is the rule "texts for conditions that also exist in the installer MUST be the installer's texts" consistent with texts that name the computer or the USB cable (for example the next step of `E-INS-26`, "check the clock of the computer"), which do not apply on the reader? [Conflict, Spec §FR-019; `docs/installer-rules.md`]
- [ ] CHK021 Are the store-only conditions that get an `E-STO-nn` id listed (wrong clock, low battery, launcher fallback, and so on), or is the set left open while the success criteria promise a message for each? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the maximum length of a message defined so that all three parts fit on one screen without paging, and is it said what is cut first when a rule id, a path and a next step do not fit? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK023 Are the buttons of an error message defined (close only, retry, open the log) and is it stated whether a message stays available after it was closed (log screen entry, last message)? [Gap, Spec §FR-019, §FR-039]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the third part ("what to do") defined for each of the three reader states ("unchanged", "restored to the previous state", "repair needed") in terms of things the user can do on the reader itself, and is the wrong-clock message specified down to the format of the date it shows? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-019]

## Offline Browsing

- [ ] CHK025 Is "offline" defined: Wi-Fi off, Wi-Fi on without internet, or no refresh tapped? The spec says the store switches Wi-Fi on for a user action, so is it clear what the list shows and which buttons it offers before any action? [Ambiguity, Spec §Story 1 scenario 5, §FR-001, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK026 Is it specified whether Install, Update and Check are shown and enabled on the cached list, and whether tapping Install on an old cached entry first refreshes the catalog or uses the cached signed entry as it is? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK027 Is "last updated <date>" consistent with a wrong reader clock (the date is the reader's own, which is exactly what may be wrong), and is the catalog's generation date shown anywhere the user browses? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-038, §Edge Cases "clock"]
- [ ] CHK028 Are the three offline start states each given a screen: cached catalog valid, no catalog yet, cached catalog discarded because its signature check failed? Is the difference visible to the user? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, §FR-012, §Edge Cases]

## States of the App List

- [ ] CHK029 Is the list's own wording consistent: FR-008 and Story 1 say "exactly one of the four states", yet apps not in the catalog get a fifth label, "not in the catalog", and notes are added; is the difference between state, note and label defined? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, §Story 1 scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK030 Is each state shown by text and not only by position, grey tone or icon, since the screen has no colour? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK031 Is there a table of the actions offered per state and per note (install, update, remove, check, none), and does it cover the store's own entry, a pending repair, and an installed version that was withdrawn? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK032 Is it stated where "update available" shows both versions (list row or detail page), and where the user sees that an update of the store is prepared and takes effect at the next opening? [Gap, Spec §Story 3 scenario 1, §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the order in which several notes appear defined (for example "update available" together with "changed since install" and "from a local file"), and is the row's room for them bounded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]

## Restart Wording and Device Facts

- [ ] CHK034 Is the request to say "plainly whether the reader has to be restarted" reconciled with the rule to say that it "may" have to be restarted, and is it said why the plain form is not yet possible? [Conflict, Spec §FR-018, §Background device facts]
- [ ] CHK035 Does the spec define what each verified outcome changes in the wording (restart needed, not needed, entry shown without restart, behavior for a missing file), and in which texts, so that the change can be checked and not only "changed in one place"? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions "device facts", §SC-011]
- [ ] CHK036 Are the wording rules defined for every operation that changes what the reader shows: install, update, remove, adopt (a record only, so presumably nothing to restart), a repair that changed the desktop configuration, and the self-update (the next opening of PB Store, not a restart of the reader)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the difference between "restart the reader" and "open PB Store again" kept clear in the texts, and are the steps to restart the reader (or a pointer to them) part of the requirement? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK038 Is "noticeably longer" for the next start of the reader quantified from the observation, or is the observation's source cited (research §18 of feature 002), so the claim is not stronger than the evidence? [Clarity, Spec §Background, §FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria and Traceability

- [ ] CHK039 Do the success criteria cover the e-ink requirements beyond SC-009 (paging position, refresh behavior, progress update rate, message length, readable text size, restart wording equal to the verified facts)? [Coverage, Spec §SC-001, §SC-005, §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK040 Is "the look follows PB Notes (feature 010) and PB Cloud" checkable from this repository (a short list of the elements that are required: top bar, rounded dialogs, paged lists), or does it depend on documents that are not here? [Dependency, Measurability, Spec §FR-042]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`

- Link to relevant resources or documentation
